name: Solo Run Fest 2026
short_description: Solo Run Fest 2026 was a point-to-point half marathon, 10 km and 5 km held on 27 September 2026 in Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia, from Stadion Manahan to Taman Balekambang.
ai_summary: Solo Run Fest 2026 was held on Sunday 27 September 2026 in Surakarta (Solo), Central Java, Indonesia, on a point-to-point course from Stadion Manahan to Taman Balekambang. It offered a 21.1 km half marathon with a 3 hour 45 minute cut-off, a 10 km, a 5 km and a 5 km student category, with entry from Rp 200,000 (5 km student) to Rp 650,000 (half marathon). The provincial government reported about 7,000 runners, up from about 5,000 in 2025.

core_facts.venue: Stadion Manahan (start) to Taman Balekambang (finish), Surakarta

pros: Generous half-marathon limit of 3 hours 45 minutes
Water every 2 to 3 km; nine stations on the half-marathon map, with fruit and sponges
Route through Solo's heritage centre, certified by PASI in 2025
Finish at Taman Balekambang sits next to the start at Stadion Manahan
Rp393.5 million prize pool with national and master categories
cons: The half marathon climbs the Manahan overpass twice
Flag-off times were not published before the 2026 race
Tight first checkpoint: 5 km within 50 minutes
No refunds, no transfers and no race-day pack collection

excerpt_quotes.quote: Seru banget. Banyak yang ikut. Acaranya seru. Rute flyover cukup menantang karena menanjak.
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Runner Nanda (Madiun), quoted in Jawa Tengah provincial government news report on Solo Run Fest 2025

excerpt_quotes.quote: Rutenya enak, ada jalan yang memiliki elevasi, ada yang datar. Harapannya ke depan untuk sterilisasi jalurnya saja agar lebih nyaman bagi pelari
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Runner Darwis (traveled from Yogyakarta), quoted in Tribun Solo advertorial coverage

excerpt_quotes.quote: Acara mantap, pesertanya banyak, refreshment juga lengkap. Flyover menantang karena menanjak.
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Amikom Solo students Nanda and Juni, quoted in Kebumen Update

research_highlights: Start at Stadion Manahan Solo, finish at Taman Balekambang; the 2026 edition offered a half marathon, 10K, 5K and a 5K student category
Early morning start times reported for the 2025 edition: 10K around 05:30 WIB and 5K around 05:50 WIB
Course includes a flyover (jalan layang) section that multiple runners described as challenging due to the incline, alongside flatter stretches
The 2025 edition drew about 5,000 participants, according to the mayor and Tempo (the provincial government put it at about 6,000); about 7,000 ran in 2026
Beyond the run itself, the event includes a UMKM (small business) bazaar, sportswear expo, and live music performances at the festival area
research_watchouts: A runner who traveled from Yogyakarta suggested organizers improve route sterilization (crowd/traffic control) to make the course more comfortable for participants
The flyover climb was repeatedly singled out by participants as the toughest part of the route due to its ascent

faqs.question: When is Solo Run Fest 2026 taking place?
faqs.answer: Solo Run Fest 2026 was held on Sunday 27 September 2026 in Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia. The organiser did not publish flag-off times, but its cut-off points imply a 5am half-marathon start. Race packs were collected at Taman Balekambang on 25 and 26 September, not on race day.

faqs.question: What distances are offered at Solo Run Fest 2026?
faqs.answer: Four categories over three distances: a 21.1 km half marathon, a 10 km, a 5 km and a 5 km student category. Entry fees were Rp 200,000 for the 5 km student race, Rp 350,000 for the 5 km, Rp 450,000 for the 10 km and Rp 650,000 for the half marathon, with a 3 hour 45 minute half cut-off.

faqs.question: Where is Solo Run Fest 2026 held?
faqs.answer: In Surakarta (Solo), Central Java. The course was point to point, starting at Stadion Manahan and finishing at Taman Balekambang, and the half-marathon route used the Manahan overpass twice and passed Taman Sriwedari, Pura Mangkunegaran and Solo Balapan station. Water stations were set every 2 to 3 km.
